summary.headline: Alembic Q1 FY27 revenue rose 26% YoY to INR2,150 crore; FY27 growth outlook raised to closer to mid-teens on US Generics strength.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 26% YoY to INR2,150 crore, with India Branded up 7%, International Generics up 37% and API up 33%. Reported EBITDA rose 21% to INR348 crore (16% margin), PBT grew 17% to INR223 crore and PAT grew 12% to INR173 crore, with a higher effective tax rate of about 22%. US Generics growth guidance was raised to mid-to-high teens from low-to-mid teens, lifting overall FY27 growth outlook to closer to mid-teens from low double digits. Management kept the roughly 150 bps FY27 margin dilution guidance from the early US branded launch (Pivya) and said US branded breakeven is targeted around year-end.

segments.name: US Generics
segments.commentary: Grew 49% YoY in INR, predominantly volume-driven, with Bosutinib (one month of sales, launched June) and about six to seven Q1 launches contributing. Ex-Bosutinib US business grew about 25%. Guidance raised to mid-to-high teens growth.

segments.name: US Branded Specialty (Pivya and two smaller UTI-related products)
segments.commentary: Soft launch in first three months, a drag on margins with no manufacturing capex (CMO-sourced, field force and marketing spend only). Management targets breakeven by around year-end and positive contribution from FY28.

segments.name: India Branded
segments.commentary: Grew 7% YoY. Animal Health grew 24% (about 22% of India business), while acute (about 37% of India business) remains a drag. Specialty is about 60% of total revenue; Gynae, Gastro and Ophthal growing in line with market. India guidance for FY27 is growth closer to market, high single digit per management.

segments.name: International Generics (ex-US, ROW)
segments.commentary: Grew 37% YoY, with growth across markets. Management guided about 15% INR growth for the year; opened Latin American territories and announced JV in Saudi Arabia and Canada activity.

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: Grew 33% YoY, volume-led. FY27 guidance of about 10% growth was described as likely to be at or slightly above that level.

guidance_outlook: FY27 overall growth outlook raised to closer to mid-teens from low double digits; US Generics now mid-to-high teens (from low-to-mid teens), other business guidance unchanged.

FY27 EBITDA margin: core business operating leverage to lift core margin toward high teens, partially offset by about 150 bps dilution from US branded for the full year; reported margin expected broadly flat to slightly better than FY26's 16%.
Gross margin guided within 70-75% range; Q1 was similar QoQ with solvent price increases, product mix and an Ophthaline debottlenecking shutdown weighing.
US branded breakeven targeted around end of FY27 (Q4 or Q1 FY28), positive contribution from FY28.
Gross debt to fall back to at least March levels in Q2-Q3, with a longer-term aim of around 1x EBITDA; interest cost expected to decline.
Roughly 15 more US launches over the remaining nine months of FY27 and a similar number in FY28.
capex_capacity: Ophthaline facility preventive debottlenecking and upgrade taken in Q1 FY27; expanded capacity without incremental capex but caused under-absorption.
About INR400 crore of capex added in the last year, per management.
Ongoing investments in manufacturing capabilities, debottlenecking and capacity enhancement; peptide development programme progressing.
Intangible assets from US branded product acquisitions capitalised in Q4 FY26, amortised over about 7-8 years; about 70-75% of the YoY depreciation increase attributed to intangibles.
demand_pricing: US growth in Q1 was predominantly volume-driven despite ongoing pricing pressure; management expects price erosion to be a watch item.
Bosutinib exclusivity (180 days, 100mg and 500mg strengths) runs until November; low-volume indication with good pricing; no competitor seen yet.
Management views the ex-Bosutinib US base run-rate (about USD 75-76 mn per quarter implied) as the new normal for a quarter or two, subject to erosion.
Non-US exports (ROW, B2B) guided to grow about 15% in INR; management says quarterly variance is possible.
INR depreciation is supporting pricing according to management; not broken out for US revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What drove US Q1 growth beyond Bosutinib and how long is exclusivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Ex-Bosutinib US business grew about 25% on new launches (six to seven in Q1 plus some from Q4); exclusivity on 100mg and 500mg runs until November, and about 15 more launches are planned for the rest of the year.

qa_highlights.question: When will the US branded business (Pivya) contribute positively to EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Soft launch with J-curve; breakeven targeted around year-end trend, positive contribution from next financial year. No hardware capex; spend is field force and marketing only, with product made by a CMO.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 EBITDA margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Core margin improvement toward high teens partly offset by about 150 bps US branded dilution; management said it is safer to assume margin close to high teens, with reported margin broadly flat to slightly better than FY26 16%. Q1 dilution was higher than 150 bps, which management confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the India Branded outlook and when will human health recover?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 India guidance is close to market growth, high single digit per management, aiming to close the gap. Human health recovery expected in a quarter or two after new sales head Ramesh Juneja joined; gastro, ophthal and cardio growing double digits, acute dragging.

qa_highlights.question: What is the API and ROW outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: API expected to be around the 10% growth guided, possibly slightly above. ROW guided at about 15% INR growth; management said guidance is set at what it is confident of delivering.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gross debt and interest cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt about INR1,600 crore, above March due to higher receivables; expected to unwind in Q2-Q3 with debt reduction and interest cost to decline.

risks_watch: US price erosion and possible share loss on the base business; management says it is unclear how Q2 onward will develop.
Bosutinib revenue is uncertain after November exclusivity ends, with competition expected to be drastic given low volumes.
US branded (Pivya) drag on margins may exceed the guided 150 bps in the ramp phase; breakeven timing depends on sales ramp.
Gross margin pressure from solvent prices (Middle East), product mix and under-absorption from the Ophthaline shutdown.
Working capital and receivables: debt at about INR1,600 crore, with reduction targeted in Q2-Q3.
Acute portfolio and human health India recovery depend on management changes taking a few quarters.
summary.management_tone: Confident on US Generics and the raised top-line outlook, but more cautious and hedged on US branded profitability timing, margin trajectory and Bosutinib sustainability beyond November; several answers were framed as "work in progress" or "hope" statements.
key_quotes: At the beginning of the year, we had indicated that the US Generics could grow in the low to mid-teens based on the performance and the trends we're seeing in Q1
So I think the main thing for the US business to grow, you have to have meaningful launches coming up.
So we should see a similar trajectory of operating margin getting maintained at an overall level as we see operating leverage playing out.

financial_highlights.change: +12% YoY; effective tax rate about 22% vs about 19% a year ago (new tax regime migration)

financial_highlights.value: Grew 49% YoY in INR; about 37-38% constant currency (about 10 pts currency benefit per management)

financial_highlights.change: Above March level due to higher receivables

adds.what: Ophthaline facility preventive debottlenecking and upgrade (expanded capacity, no incremental capex)
About INR400 crore of capex added over the last year (capacity not specified)

growth.why: Management raised FY27 consolidated growth to closer to mid-teens (from low double digits) and US Generics to mid-to-high teens, backed mainly by volume-led US launches (about six to seven in Q1, Bosutinib) and ~15 more US launches over the remaining nine months, with no specific new capacity commissioned beyond a debottlenecking and about INR400 crore of recent capex.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Core margin guided toward high teens from operating leverage, but ~150 bps Pivya dilution (Q1 dilution was above 150 bps) keeps reported EBITDA margin broadly flat to slightly better than FY26's 16%; Q1 margin was 16%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant or line discussed; Ophthaline was debottlenecked without incremental capex, and about INR400 crore of capex was added over the last year, with no further capacity timetable given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: US Generics guided to mid-to-high teens INR growth with ~15 more US launches over the remaining nine months, and Q1 US growth was predominantly volume-driven (+49% INR, ex-Bosutinib about +25%).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management described capex as already added (about INR400 crore) and the Ophthaline debottlenecking as done without incremental capex; no new capex plan or board approval was stated, and utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 consolidated growth was already raised to closer to mid-teens from low double digits and US to mid-to-high teens, but API (~10%) and ROW (~15%) guidance were held and Bosutinib exclusivity ends in November.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management said it is unclear how Q2 onward will develop given US price erosion, Bosutinib revenue faces drastic competition after November exclusivity, and Pivya drag could exceed 150 bps; gross margin pressure from solvent prices.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: About 15 more US launches are planned over the remaining nine months of FY27 and a similar number in FY28, with Pivya and two UTI products already launched.

rows.label: US branded (Pivya) breakeven
rows.why: Breakeven targeted around year-end with positive contribution from FY28, but soft launch with J-curve and margin drag may exceed 150 bps, so timing depends on the sales ramp.

rows.label: Gross debt back to March levels
rows.why: Gross debt was about INR1,600 crore at June 2026, above March due to receivables, and management expects it to return to at least March levels with interest cost declining.

rows.label: India human health recovery
rows.why: Acute (about 37% of India business) is dragging and India Branded grew only 7%; recovery is expected a quarter or two after new sales head joined, with FY27 India guidance at high single digit.

tone.note: Management was confident on US Generics volume, launches and the raised top-line outlook, but hedged on Pivya breakeven timing, margin trajectory, and Bosutinib and price erosion beyond November; analysts pressed on those points.
